target.name: Titanium dioxide, chloride process, at plant

strategy.label: top-down model drafted from the report excerpt by the LLM pipeline (reverse-bafu draft); the report's tables are published comparison data, not this dataset's inventory
strategy.note: basis: per 1 kg of TiO2; Tab. 85.3 is headed 'Kg per kg of product', Tab. 85.5 'Consumption per kg of product (MJ/kg)', Tab. 85.7 and Tab. 85.9 'Gram per kg of product'. The CHLORIDE-process column is used.; allocation: none stated for the TiO2 process itself; 6 of 7 inputs carry a printed amount, 1 a printed range, 0 no number in the report. Review every derivation; unreviewed entries have reviewed_by = null.

gaps_reported_by_model: Section 85.6 says 'This inventory is based on confidential information provided by industry sources. The input information may not be divulged.' The printed BAT-Notes figures are what the report compares against, not necessarily the exact dataset amounts.
No transport, no infrastructure (chemical plant) and no water input are quantified anywhere in the excerpt for the TiO2 process; they are therefore not included.
Tab. 85.5 gives no coal for the chloride process and no breakdown of which fuel produces the steam beyond the sentence about a natural gas boiler.
The excerpt gives no process water, no NOx and no organic emissions for the chloride route.
skipped_items: Titanium dioxide, chloride process, at plant: product — Reference product; the whole excerpt is per kg of product.

node.name: Titanium dioxide, chloride process, at plant, disaggregated
node.comment: drafted from 2007 - LCI chemicals - Althaus.pdf pp. 845-847

inputs.name: Rutile, 95% titanium dioxide, at plant
inputs.note: Chloride-process precursor. The text adds 'The chloride process titanium dioxide is also assumed to stem from ilmenite, although in fact rutile, synthetic rutile and /or beneficiate are used. The data for mining of ilmenite are taken from (BUWAL 232).' so the supplying dataset is the ilmenite/rutile ore, not TiO2 itself.

derivation.quote: Synthetic rutile   ng   1.06   (Chemlink.com)   [Tab. 85.3 precursors for TiO2 production, chloride-process column, 'Kg per kg of product']
derivation.mapping_reason: Tab. 85.3 names 'Synthetic rutile' for the chloride route; the rutile concentrate is that material, while ilmenite is the lower-grade ore the sulfate route uses.

inputs.name: Chlorine, liquid, production mix, at plant
inputs.note: Printed value for the chloride process.

derivation.quote: Chlorine   na   0.18   (UBA BAT Notes, 2001)   [Tab. 85.3 precursors for TiO2 production, chloride-process column]
derivation.mapping_reason: Exact substance and a production mix, as the report gives no specific electrolysis route; chlorine dioxide is a different chemical.

inputs.name: xxx Electricity, medium voltage, production UCTE, at grid
inputs.note: 1.51 MJ (TiO2 manufacture) + 0.83 MJ (follow-up treatment) = 2.34 MJ/kg, the two columns of the same row. The text says the model facility 'imports UCTE grid electricity'.

derivation.quote: Electric energy   1.51   0.83   [Tab. 85.5 energy consumption for TiO2 production (chloride process), TiO2 manufacture + Follow-up treatment]
derivation.factor_source: 1 kWh = 3.6 MJ, so MJ x 0.2778 = kWh (ecoinvent convention)
derivation.mapping_reason: The report says the model plant 'imports UCTE grid electricity'; this is the UCTE production mix, beating the single-fuel UCTE variants and the RER/CH grids.

inputs.name: Heat, natural gas, at industrial furnace 1MW
inputs.note: 1.7 + 7.7 = 9.4 MJ/kg. The text: 'The model facility portrayed here uses natural gas in a boiler to produce steam', so the steam is entered as natural-gas heat in MJ.

derivation.quote: Steam   1.7   7.7   [Tab. 85.5 energy consumption for TiO2 production (chloride process)]
derivation.mapping_reason: The report: 'uses natural gas in a boiler to produce steam'; this is delivered heat in MJ from a natural-gas furnace, which matches the MJ/kg the table gives, beating the 'burned in' variants that model the combustion itself.

inputs.name: Natural gas, burned in industrial furnace 1MW
inputs.note: 2.9 + 4.2 = 7.1 MJ/kg of direct process gas, separate from the gas burned for steam.

derivation.quote: Gas   2.9   4.2   [Tab. 85.5 energy consumption for TiO2 production (chloride process)]
derivation.mapping_reason: Direct process gas burned on site, which is what the separate 'Gas' row of Tab. 85.5 is, as opposed to the gas that makes the steam.

inputs.name: xx Disposal, residue from TiO2 prod. Cl, 56% water, to residual material landfill
inputs.note: 0.11 + 2.25 = 2.36 g/kg. Treated here as a disposal service (an input), since the report lists it under wastewater emissions but it is a solid residue. Low confidence on which disposal dataset applies.

derivation.quote: Filter residues   0.11   2.25   [Tab. 85.9 wastewater emissions for TiO2 production (chloride process)]
derivation.factor_source: gram -> kilogram (the table header reads 'Gram per kg of product')
derivation.mapping_reason: The disposal dataset made for exactly this residue stream of the chloride route, beating the SO4 variant and the generic residue landfills.

inputs.name: xx Disposal, residue from TiO2 prod. Cl, 56% water, to residual material landfill
inputs.note: The excerpt gives 184 g/kg from the BAT notes and says industry suggests up to 1 kg/kg; entered as a bounded free input over exactly that printed range.

derivation.quote: Chloride process. According to (UBA BAT Notes, 2001), chloride process sludges total 184 g / kg product. Industry sources however suggest somewhat higher values, ranging up to 1 kg / kg product
derivation.factor_source: gram -> kilogram (the table header reads 'Gram per kg of product')
derivation.mapping_reason: Same stream as the filter residues and the only chloride-route TiO2 disposal dataset in the database.

emissions.name: Particulates, unspecified
emissions.note: 0.005 g (storage) + 0.186 g (follow-up treatment) = 0.191 g/kg. The report does not state a size fraction for the chloride route.

derivation.quote: Particles   0.005   ng   ng   0.186   [Tab. 85.7 direct air emissions for TiO2 production (chloride process)]
derivation.factor_source: gram -> kilogram (the table header reads 'Gram per kg of product')
derivation.mapping_reason: The only candidate; the report states no particle size fraction for TiO2, so the unspecified particulate flow is the honest choice.

emissions.name: Hydrogen Chloride
emissions.note: The asterisk in the table marks 0.024 g/kg as the value the report actually uses for the model chloride plant.

derivation.quote: HCl   ng   0.007   0.024 *   ng   * This value is used for the model chloride plant.   [Tab. 85.7]
derivation.factor_source: gram -> kilogram (the table header reads 'Gram per kg of product')
derivation.mapping_reason: Exact substance in the stated air compartment; the soil and water copies are the wrong compartment and 'Chloride' is the ion, not HCl.

derivation.quote: SO2   ng   ng   1.68   ng   [Tab. 85.7 direct air emissions for TiO2 production (chloride process), off-gas treatment]
derivation.factor_source: gram -> kilogram (the table header reads 'Gram per kg of product')
derivation.mapping_reason: Exact substance and compartment; 'Sulfur Oxides' is the aggregate and 'Sulfur' the element.

emissions.name: Iron
emissions.note: The table prints 0.011 g/kg but the footnote below it states 'This report uses a value of 0.5 g iron per kg produced TiO2'; the footnote value is the one the dataset was built with.

derivation.quote: Iron   0.011 *   ng   ...   This report uses a value of 0.5 g iron per kg produced TiO2   [Tab. 85.9 wastewater emissions (chloride process)]
derivation.factor_source: gram -> kilogram (the table header reads 'Gram per kg of product')
derivation.mapping_reason: The report says only 'Iron' with no oxidation state, so the unspecified iron flow beats Iron(2+) and Iron(3+).

derivation.quote: Cadmium   0.00000022   ng   [Tab. 85.9 wastewater emissions for TiO2 production (chloride process)]
derivation.factor_source: gram -> kilogram (the table header reads 'Gram per kg of product')
derivation.mapping_reason: Exact substance and compartment; Cadmium(2+) presumes an oxidation state the report does not give and Cadmium-109 is a radionuclide.

derivation.quote: Mercury   0.00000022   ng   [Tab. 85.9 wastewater emissions for TiO2 production (chloride process)]
derivation.factor_source: gram -> kilogram (the table header reads 'Gram per kg of product')
derivation.mapping_reason: Exact substance and compartment; Mercury(2+) presumes a speciation the report does not give.
